name: Uzzah
overview: Uzzah was a male Levite, identified as the son of Shimei and associated with the Mahlite family, which descended from Merari, a son of Levi. His lineage places him within the priestly tribe of Levi, known for their roles in temple service and religious duties. The record of Uzzah appears in the genealogical context of 1 Chronicles 6:29-30.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzzah is a proper name meaning 'strong, fierce one.' This meaning reflects a characteristic strength but was not given directly by God. The name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:29.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Uzzah as the son of Shimei, as stated in 1 Chronicles 6:29, with an inferred relationship to Shimea mentioned in 1 Chronicles 6:30. Beyond these, no additional family relationships are documented in the given data.
scriptureSignificance: Uzzah's significance lies primarily in his identification within the Levitical lineage, specifically among the Mahlites, descendants of Merari, who had particular responsibilities in the service of the tabernacle. His mention in the genealogical records underscores the importance of priestly heritage and the continuity of Levitical service in Israel's worship practices. Though details beyond genealogy are not provided here, his place in the tribe of Levi connects him to the sacred duties entrusted to this family line.
